The '''Anne Bennett Prize''' and '''Senior Anne Bennett Prize''' are awards given by the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/lms-prize-regulations|title=LMS prizes - details and regulations {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=winners/>

In every third year, the society offers the Senior Anne Bennett prize to a mathematician normally based in the United Kingdom for work in, influence on or service to mathematics, particularly in relation to advancing the careers of women in mathematics.<ref name=":0" />

In the two years out of three in which the Senior Anne Bennett Prize is not awarded, the society offers the Anne Bennett Prize to a mathematician within ten years of their doctorate for work in and influence on mathematics, particularly acting as an inspiration for women mathematicians.<ref name=":0" />

Both prizes are awarded in memory of Anne Bennett, an administrator for the London Mathematical Society who died in 2012.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/content/lms-obituary-anne-bennett|title=LMS Obituary - Anne Bennett {{!}} London Mathematical Society|last=Nixon|first=Fiona|date=2012|website=www.lms.ac.uk|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> The prize was established in 2013 and first given in 2014.

The Anne Bennett Prizes should be distinguished from the Anne Bennett Memorial Award for Distinguished Service of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/DistinguishedService/|title=The Anne Bennett Memorial Award for Distinguished Service|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref> for which Anne Bennett also worked.<ref name=":1" />

==Anne Bennett Prize Winners==
The winners of the Anne Bennett Prize have been:
* 2015 [[Apala Majumdar]], in recognition of her outstanding contributions to the mathematics of liquid crystals and to the liquid crystal community.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/citations-lms-prize-winners|title=Citations for 2015 LMS prize winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=ams15/>
* 2016 [[Julia Wolf]], in recognition of her outstanding contributions to additive number theory, combinatorics and harmonic analysis and to the mathematical community.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/2016-nominations-lms-prizes|title=2016 LMS Prize Winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=ams16/>
* 2018 [[Lotte Hollands]], in recognition of her outstanding research at the interface between quantum theory and geometry and of her leadership in mathematical outreach activities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/29062018-1745/2018-lms-prize-winners|title=2018 LMS Prize Winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=ams18/>
*2019 [[Eva-Maria Graefe]], in recognition of her outstanding research in quantum theory and the inspirational role she has played among female students and early career researchers in mathematics and physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/2019-nominations-lms-prizes|title=2019 LMS Prize Winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref>
*2021 [[Viveka Erlandsson]], "for her outstanding achievements in geometry and topology and her inspirational active role in promoting women mathematicians".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/Erlandsson%20%28Anne%20Bennett%29.pdf|title=Anne Bennett Prize: citation for Viveka Erlandsson|publisher=London Mathematical Society|year=2021|access-date=2022-02-04}}</ref>
*2022 [[Asma Hassannezhad]], "for her outstanding work in spectral geometry and her substantial contributions toward the advancement of women in mathematics."<ref>{{cite web |title=LMS Prize Winners 2022 {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/lms-prize-winners-2022 |website=www.lms.ac.uk |access-date=21 August 2022}}</ref>
*2024 [[Ana Ros Camacho]], "for her ground-breaking work on categorical proofs of the Landau–Ginzburg/Conformal Field Theory correspondence and her tireless dedication to the advancement of women in [[mathematical physics]]"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news/2024-lms-prize-winners|title=2024 LMS Prize Winners|publisher=London Mathematical Society|year=2024|access-date=2024-06-28}}</ref>
*2025 [[Henna Koivusalo]], "for her work on cut-and-project sets, dynamical systems and fractals and her dedication to the advancement of women in mathematics."<ref>{{cite web |title=LMS Prize Winners 2025 {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news/lms-prize-winners-2025 |website=www.lms.ac.uk |access-date=4 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Henna Koivusalo wins LMS Anne Bennett Prize |url=https://www.bristol.ac.uk/maths/news/2025/henna-koivusalo-wins-lms-anne-bennett-prize-.html#:~:text=The%20Anne%20Bennett%20Prize%20is,an%20inspiration%20for%20women%20mathematicians. |website=University of Bristol |access-date=7 July 2025}}</ref>

==Senior Anne Bennett Prize Winners==
The winners of the Senior Anne Bennett Prize have been:
* 2014 [[Caroline Series]], in recognition of her leading contributions to hyperbolic geometry and [[symbolic dynamics]], and of the major impact of her numerous initiatives towards the advancement of women in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/lms-prizes-2014|title=LMS Prizes 2014 {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=ams14/>
* 2017 [[Alison Etheridge]], in recognition of her outstanding research on measure-valued stochastic processes and applications to population biology; and for her impressive leadership and service to the profession.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/30062017-1833/lms-prizes-2017|title=LMS Prizes 2017 {{!}} London Mathematical Society|website=www.lms.ac.uk|access-date=2019-10-08}}</ref><ref name=ams17/>
* 2020 [[Peter Clarkson]], "in recognition of his tireless work to support gender equality in UK mathematics, and particularly for his leadership in developing good practice among departments of mathematical sciences".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/Clarkson_Snr%20Anne%20Bennett_citation.pdf|title=Senior Anne Bennett Prize citation: Peter Clarkson|publisher=London Mathematical Society|date=2020|accessdate=2020-06-27}}</ref>
* 2023 [[Eugénie Hunsicker]], "for her outstanding work to improve equality and diversity in the mathematical community and for the depth of her mathematical achievements across an impressive range of areas, from L2 [[Hodge theory]] to data science."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/2023-lms-prize-winners|title=2023 LMS Prize Winners|publisher=London Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-08-28}}</ref>
